words.name: Boeckenfoerde
words.description: Ernst-Wolfgang Boeckenfoerde, author of the dilemma that the liberal state lives on preconditions it cannot itself guarantee

words.name: confidence
words.description: Subjective probability (0 to 1) that the tagged estimate range contains the true value.

words.name: value
words.description: a stored number; reference the provenance qualifier triple, not this bare word

triples.name: power reduction claim
triples.description: reducing the power of powerful actors is usually a net benefit, not a harm

triples.name: distribution impossibility premise
triples.description: no actor can ensure even distribution of power: the act of relinquishing power removes the capacity to guarantee the distribution's outcome

triples.name: self-undermining transfer
triples.description: logical structure in which executing the transfer destroys the enforcement capacity for the transfer's goal

triples.name: boeckenfoerde dilemma
triples.description: the liberal state lives on preconditions it cannot itself guarantee; static analogue of the premise

triples.name: self-enforcing equilibrium
triples.description: even distribution can persist only as a coordination equilibrium among many actors, not as a guaranteed state

triples.name: power reconcentration
triples.description: distributed power tends to reconcentrate over time (iron law of oligarchy)

triples.name: continuous reduction strategy
triples.description: because even distribution is neither achievable in one act nor stable, ongoing marginal reduction of concentrated power is the second-best strategy

triples.name: power vacuum risk
triples.description: abrupt power reduction can transfer power to worse actors instead of counterweights

triples.name: historical transition failure
triples.description: post-abdication collapse cases: Sulla's restored republic, Diocletian's tetrarchy

triples.name: confidence value
triples.description: The p-value of an assumed value: the subjective probability between 0 and 1 that the tagged estimate is right.

values.description: probability that no single actor can guarantee even power distribution, given the self-undermining structure of the transfer
probability that marginal reduction of concentrated power toward counterweights yields net benefit; raised from 0.7 in v0.0.1 because the revised premise supports the second-best argument
probability that distributed power reconcentrates absent active counterbalancing
probability that the Sulla and Diocletian cases show abdication without outcome guarantee
